094D.flag: Failed the phase-sign test T3: the zones read +23.5 mm/yr against far stable ground, where they should sink. Unwrapping is ruled out, and neither the ECMWF weather model nor NASA's own troposphere screens (in the product) remove it; the signal covers the whole valley. Our own pairs from NISAR's raw single-look data reduce it to +3.5 mm/yr (still failing). Shown for inspection, not interpretation (notebooks/03/t3_094d_checks.json). Summer to autumn only: with June to October dates alone, a seasonal cycle can bias its rate by about half (test T6, notebooks/03/t5_t6_synthetic.json).

compare.reason: Side by side, each satellite in its own line of sight. Tracks are paired by geometry (NISAR 129A with Sentinel-1 007D: both see east-west motion the same way). The verdict per zone comes from the automatic checks.

z3.label: Historically subsiding · 2026 trend inconclusive
z3.detail: EGMS history shows this zone sinking, but the 2026 Sentinel-1 evidence is limited: no connected ascending (029A) series in July to October, and the descending (007D) result changes sign across processing runs. Over January to November no zone pixel stays connected on either track.

s1:029A.label: Local reference sensitivity
s1:029A.detail: On 029A, terrain near the zones also shows a negative line-of-sight signal, so part of a zone value may come from the reference area, the atmosphere or the geometry rather than the zone. The values are shown as measured, without a correction.

egms.label: EGMS Ortho · 2020–2025 · 100 m
egms.detail: Tile E54N25, 9 December 2020–25 November 2025. Zone 3 shows the strongest historical sinking in this report. Its 2026 trend is inconclusive. Cell maps and time series are pending. The R05 stable-ground sample uses a different mask from the Sentinel-1 outer comparison area.

methods.s1: Sentinel-1 IW2 VV bursts 029_060407_IW2 and 007_013694_IW2, processed by ASF HyP3 (10×2 looks, water mask) and inverted on a 40 m grid with coherence-squared weights. Each pair is zeroed on a terrain reference band 3 to 6.5 km from the zone edges; the outer comparison area is 6.5 to 8 km. Not GNSS-calibrated.
methods.sign: Line of sight, positive toward the satellite. Red is away from the satellite, blue is toward.
methods.rate: A rate is a fitted annualized slope over the window, not a long-term velocity. No per-pixel uncertainty layer is validated yet.
methods.nisar: NISAR L2 GUNW (frequency A, HH, 80 m) streamed over the 50 km window by fetch.py: mask decoded as a bitfield, largest connected component, ionosphere screen subtracted. stack.py: coherence ≥ 0.35, elevation slope and stable-ground reference removed per pair, small-baseline inversion with one group per side of the January to June gap, rate through the dates. calibrate.py ties each track to EuVeM2022 on stable ground. Beta and provisional products, not intended for scientific research.
methods.zones: Four zone circles from the advisor's starter kit (permission to publish them is still to be confirmed).
